title: OpenAI Dark Promotion Restrictions on Chinese Open Source Models: Huang Renxun and Musk Unite to Counterattack: Openness Will Prevail

content_html:
A heated Silicon Valley debate over the open-source route of AI has intensified this week. According to The New York Times, OpenAI and Anthropic are lobbying regulators in Washington, citing national security and AI safety, to push for restrictions on China's open-source AI models. Meanwhile, NVIDIA CEO Huang Renxun, Microsoft CEO Nadella, Musk, Zuckerberg, and Google CEO Pichai have publicly taken sides supporting open source, marking the formal confrontation between the two camps.

The core of the dispute lies in the rapid rise of China's open-source AI models. Recently, Zhipu and Yuezhidan have launched open-source models that can rival the leading American models, causing concern among OpenAI and Anthropic executives who feel their competitive edge is slipping away. The two companies claim that Chinese companies are improperly acquiring their system data to develop models and should not be allowed to do so. However, industry giants like Microsoft and NVIDIA rely on open source to drive cloud services and chip demand, believing that openness and sharing are the cornerstone of technological advancement and security, and that restricting open source would only further consolidate the dominance of top companies.

Nearly 200 startups have joined forces, splitting Silicon Valley into two factions

The force supporting open source is rapidly gathering. On Wednesday, nearly 200 Silicon Valley startups signed an open letter under the name "Small Tech Association," urging the U.S. government not to restrict access to Chinese open-source AI models. On Friday, Huang Renxun posted on X platform, "The world needs both cutting-edge closed-source models and cutting-edge open-source models," and nine minutes later, Musk replied in support: "Huang Renxun is right, I fully support it." Zuckerberg also wrote, "Open source is a positive and important force," and Pichai subsequently announced that Google had also signed the open letter.

Venture capitalist Bill Gurley's summary was spot-on: "One side wants OpenAI and Anthropic to control everything, while the other is everyone else, including customers." Four informed sources revealed that U.S. officials currently favor treating Chinese open-source models as a separate national security issue rather than issuing a comprehensive ban. Meanwhile, OpenAI CEO Altman publicly expressed support for open source, but his allies were quietly lobbying behind the scenes to push for restrictions - Google and Amazon chose to stay out of the issue.

content_html_zh:
硅谷关于人工智能开源路线的激烈争论本周愈演愈烈。 据《纽约时报》报道，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 正在以国家安全和人工智能安全为由游说华盛顿监管机构，推动对中国开源人工智能模型的限制。 与此同时，英伟达CEO黄仁勋、微软CEO纳德拉、马斯克、扎克伯格以及谷歌CEO皮查伊都公开表明支持开源的立场，标志着两大阵营的正式对抗。

争议的核心在于中国开源人工智能模型的快速崛起。 最近，智浦和月之蛋推出了可以与美国领先模型相媲美的开源模型，引起了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 高管的担忧，他们认为他们的竞争优势正在消失。 两家公司声称，中国公司不正当地获取其系统数据来开发模型，不应允许其这样做。 然而，微软、英伟达等行业巨头依靠开源来拉动云服务和芯片需求，认为开放和共享是技术进步和安全的基石，限制开源只会进一步巩固顶级公司的主导地位。

近200家初创公司联手，硅谷分裂成两派

支持开源的力量正在迅速聚集。 周三，近200家硅谷初创公司以“小型科技协会”的名义签署了一封公开信，敦促美国政府不要限制对中国开源人工智能模型的访问。 周五，黄仁勋在X平台发文，“这个世界既需要最前沿的闭源模型，也需要最前沿的开源模型”，9分钟后，马斯克回复支持：“黄仁勋说得对，我完全支持。” 扎克伯格还写道，“开源是一股积极而重要的力量”，皮查伊随后宣布谷歌也签署了这封公开信。

风险投资家 Bill Gurley 的总结一语中的：“一方面希望 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 控制一切，另一方面则是其他所有人，包括客户。” 四名知情人士透露，美国官员目前倾向于将中国开源模式视为单独的国家安全问题，而不是发布全面禁令。 与此同时，OpenAI 首席执行官 Altman 公开表示支持开源，但他的盟友却在幕后悄悄游说，推动限制——谷歌和亚马逊选择置身事外。
